summary: Chinese has two demonstratives: 这 zhè ‘this’ (near) and 那 nà ‘that’ (far). They never change for gender, number or case. Before a noun they need a measure word: 这个人 ‘this person’, 那本书 ‘that book’. The plural is 这些 / 那些 ‘these / those’, without a measure word: 这些人. Alone as a subject they stand bare: 这是老师 ‘this is the teacher’. The place words are 这里 ‘here’ and 那里 ‘there’ (northern 这儿 / 那儿).

blocks.caption: This and that
这 / 那 + measure word + noun

blocks.title: No measure word after 这些 / 那些
blocks.text: 这些书 — not *这些本书. 些 is itself a measure word (‘some’).

blocks.title: 那 or 哪?
blocks.text: 那 nà ‘that’ (4th tone) and 哪 nǎ ‘which?’ (3rd tone, with 口) — likewise 那里 ‘there’ and 哪里 ‘where?’.

items.title: As subject: no measure word
points: 这是老师。 This is the teacher.
那是门。 That is the door.

items.title: Before a noun: measure word
points: 这位老师在这里。 This teacher is here.

blocks.title: zhèi and nèi
blocks.text: Many northerners say zhèi / nèi before a measure word: 这个 zhèige, 那个 nèige.

askYourself: Near me or away from me? → 这 or 那.
One thing or several? → 这 / 那 + measure word, or 这些 / 那些 (no measure word).
Is the demonstrative alone as the subject (‘this is …’)? → bare 这 / 那: 这是…
Is it a noun phrase (‘this book’)? → 这 + measure word + noun: 这本书.
Do I mean a place? → 这里 / 那里 (这儿 / 那儿).
steps: Add the noun’s measure word (or 些 for the plural).

traps: *这书 in careful speech → 这本书.
*这些个人 / *这些本书 → 这些人, 这些书.
那里 nàli ‘there’ ≠ 哪里 nǎli ‘where?’.
这 is not an article: a thing that is simply known is a bare noun (书在这里 ‘the book is here’).

quiz.why: 这些 takes no measure word.
As a subject 这 stands alone.
那 + measure word 个 + noun; 哪个人 means ‘which person?’.
那里 nàli ‘there’; 哪里 nǎli asks ‘where?’; place needs 在.

notes.text: Greek αυτός / εκείνος agree in gender, number and case and take the article (αυτό το βιβλίο). Chinese 这 / 那 never change and take no article, but need a measure word before a noun: 这本书.
Russian этот / эта / это agree with the noun; Chinese 这 stays the same and needs a measure word: этот стол ~ 这张桌子. Это as a subject (Это книга) ~ 这是书 — but Chinese needs 是.
Spanish has three degrees (este / ese / aquel); Chinese has two: 这 for near, 那 for everything else. And 这 never agrees: este libro / esta mesa ~ 这本书 / 这张桌子.
this / that and these / those map neatly onto 这 / 那 and 这些 / 那些. The new part is the measure word in the singular: ‘this book’ is 这本书, not *这书 in careful speech, and ‘these books’ takes none: 这些书.
French ce / cette / ces agree and mark distance only optionally (-ci / -là); 这 and 那 always choose near or far, never agree, and need a measure word: cette table ~ 这张桌子.
German dieser / jener agree in gender, number and case (colloquial der da); Chinese 这 / 那 never change, but before a noun they need the measure word: dieses Buch ~ 这本书.
Hindi यह / वह are also two-way and never change for gender; they also mean ‘he / she / it’. Chinese 这 / 那 mean only ‘this / that’ and need a measure word before a noun (यह किताब ~ 这本书).
Persian in / ān stand before the noun and never change — like 这 / 那. Persian adds the classifier tā only after numbers; Chinese adds a measure word after 这 / 那 too: 这本书.
Marathi हा / ही / हे ‘this’ and तो / ती / ते ‘that’ agree in gender and number; Chinese 这 / 那 never change, but need a measure word before a noun.
Arabic hādhā / hādhihi / hāʾulāʾi agree in gender and number and the noun takes the article (hādhā l-kitāb); Chinese 这 never changes and uses a measure word instead: 这本书.
Hebrew ze / zot / ele follow the noun and need ha- on both (ha-sefer ha-ze ‘this book’); Chinese 这 + measure word comes before the noun, with no article.
Turkish bu / şu / o never change and stand before the noun (bu kitap), like 这 / 那. Turkish has a third ‘that one, look’ (şu); Chinese has two. And Chinese adds a measure word: 这本书.
Japanese この / その / あの + noun never change, like 这 / 那 — but Japanese has three distances and Chinese two (その and あの are both 那). ここ / そこ / あそこ ↔ 这里 / 那里.
Korean 이 / 그 / 저 have three distances; Chinese 这 / 那 have two. 이 책 ‘this book’ needs no counter, but Chinese puts one in: 这本书.
Finnish tämä / tuo / se decline in every case (tässä talossa ‘in this house’); 这 never changes but needs a measure word (这个房子).
Hungarian ez / az take the article and agree in case with the noun (ebben a házban ‘in this house’); Chinese 这 never changes and takes a measure word: 这个房子.
Swahili demonstratives follow the noun and agree with its class (kitabu hiki ‘this book’, vitabu hivi ‘these books’); Chinese 这 comes first, never changes and needs a measure word: 这本书.
Luganda demonstratives follow the noun and agree with its class (ekitabo kino ‘this book’); Chinese 这 stands before the noun, never changes, and takes a measure word: 这本书.
Vietnamese also needs a classifier: cái bàn này ‘this table’ ~ 这张桌子. But the Vietnamese demonstrative follows the noun (này, kia, đó); the Chinese one comes first.

Inuktitut has a large set of demonstratives for where things are — up there, down there, inside, outside, near, far — and they take case endings. Chinese has two, 这 and 那, and adds 里 for places: 这里, 那里.

seeAlso.note: dieser / diese / dieses agrees in gender, number and case; Chinese 这 never changes but needs a measure word.
Arabic hādhā / hādhihi / hāʾulāʾi change for gender and number; Chinese has one 这 and one plural 这些.
Hebrew ze / zot / ele follow the noun with ha- (ha-bayit ha-ze ‘this house’); Chinese 这 + measure word comes before the noun.
